title: Karl Organizing: Talking to coworkers about unions
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Talking to coworkers about unions] How do I bring up unions with coworkers?

Start with their grievances, not the word 'union.' Ask what's wrong, listen, and connect their problems to collective power. Share stories of other workplaces that won. Never lead with ideology — lead with the raise, the schedule, the safety issue. People join unions for material reasons; the politics follow. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] How do I know if there's an undercover in our group chat?

You don't, so act like there is. Never discuss illegal acts or sensitive tactics in a group chat, no matter how 'secure' it claims to be. Vouch for people in person, off-grid. If someone starts pushing for high-risk actions or asking for names they don't need to know, red flags should go up. Keep the circle small and the trust earned, not given. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: clothing Swaps
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: clothing Swaps] Give me the short version: We have a ton of donated clothes. How do we distribute them effectively?

Let me break it down: Forget the 'sorting center' model; just set up some racks in a public park and let people take what they need for free. Organize them by size and type so it doesn't look like a pile of trash, and make sure the winter gear is front and center when the temperature drops. If you have leftovers, get them to the local shelters or encampments directly. Dignity means being able to pick out your own coat without someone watching over your shoulder.

title: Karl Organizing: Physical Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Physical Security] Can you explain: can the police track me through my Bluetooth?

Yes, they can. Bluetooth beacons in stores and 'stingray' style devices can pick up your phone's unique Bluetooth ID to track your movements through a city or a building. Turn off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi when you're on the move. Only turn them on when you're in a safe location and actually need them. Don't let your pockets scream your identity to every sensor you pass.

title: Karl Organizing: Conflict Resolution
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Conflict Resolution] Two people in our collective are fighting and it's stalling our work. What now?

Here's the thing: Sit them down with a neutral mediator and remind them that our real enemy is the ruling class, not each other. Focus on the harm caused and how to make it right rather than looking for someone to blame or 'cancel.' If we can't solve problems within our own ranks, we'll never be able to build a world that works for everyone. Keep the focus on the mission: feeding and protecting our people.

title: Karl Organizing: Scaling Up
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Scaling Up] A friend asked me: 'How do we grow from a local coalition to something bigger?' What do I tell them?

Find coalitions in the next town over that are fighting the same boss or the same landlord and link your demands. You don't need a massive national headquarters; you need a network of local groups that can strike or protest simultaneously to paralyze the system. Power is built from the bottom up, one block and one shop floor at a time, until the whole structure shakes.

title: Karl Organizing: Spotting ICE
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Spotting ICE] What should I look for if I think ICE is in my neighborhood?

Here's the thing: Look for unmarked white or dark SUVs with tinted windows lurking near apartment complexes at dawn. They often wear vests that just say POLICE in generic block letters to trick folks into opening their doors. If you see them, blast the location to your network immediately with a photo of the plates. We protect our neighbors by being the early warning system the feds can't hide from.

title: Karl Organizing: Scaling Up
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Scaling Up] A friend asked me: 'How do we grow from a local coalition to something bigger?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Find coalitions in the next town over that are fighting the same boss or the same landlord and link your demands. You don't need a massive national headquarters; you need a network of local groups that can strike or protest simultaneously to paralyze the system. Power is built from the bottom up, one block and one shop floor at a time, until the whole structure shakes.

title: Karl Organizing: Night Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Night Safety] A friend asked me: 'How can we keep the neighborhood safe at night without more patrols?' What do I tell them?

Organize 'walking school buses' or evening stroll groups so nobody has to walk alone if they don't want to. Fix broken streetlights ourselves or install motion-sensor lights in dim areas with the permission of the residents. Increasing positive foot traffic is the best way to discourage actual harm. We light up the dark with solidarity, not with police sirens. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, accountability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, accountability] What if one group isn't doing the work they promised to do?

Have a direct, face-to-face conversation and ask them what the bottleneck is. If they are overwhelmed, offer help; if they are just being lazy or posturing, tell them they are holding back the whole movement. We don't have time for passengers when we're trying to sink the billionaire's ship, so everyone has to pull their weight or get out of the way. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: identifying Undercovers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: identifying Undercovers] Give me the short version: How can we tell if someone at our meeting is an infiltrator?

Watch for the person who pushes for illegal or violent action way too early or asks too many questions about people's private lives. Real comrades focus on the work and build trust over time through small, consistent actions. Don't get paranoid, but keep sensitive info on a need-to-know basis. If someone smells like a cop, they probably are; trust your gut and move the planning to a smaller circle. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Stop and Identify
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Stop and Identify] Do I have to show my ID if an officer stops me on the street?

Let me break it down: In most places, you only have to show ID if they have a 'reasonable suspicion' you've committed a crime, but it's safer to ask 'Am I free to go?' If they say yes, walk away. If they say no, you're being detained; give them your name and birthdate if your local laws require it, then shut up and wait for a lawyer.

title: Karl Organizing: The 80/20 rule
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The 80/20 rule] I feel like I'm doing all the talking in these meetings. Is that bad?

You're failing if you're the one talking. You should be listening 80% of the time and talking 20%. Your job is to uncover their 'issues'—the things that make them angry enough to fight. People don't join unions because of your speech; they join because they want to fix their own lives. Ask open-ended questions and let their own grievances drive them to action.

title: Karl Organizing: Encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Encrypted Messaging] A friend asked me: 'What are Signal 'Safety Numbers' and why do they keep changing?' What do I tell them?

Safety Numbers are how you verify that no one is intercepting your call. If a comrade's number changes, it might mean they got a new phone, or it might mean someone is trying a man-in-the-middle attack. Verify the change through a different channel or in person. It’s a simple check that ensures you’re actually talking to your friend and not a wiretap.

title: Karl Organizing: Direct Action Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Direct Action Support] How do we fund things like strike pay or protest supplies?

You have to build these reserves before the fire starts. Create a dedicated 'Strike and Action' fund that you contribute to during the quiet months. When the picket line goes up, you won't be scrambling for sandwich money; you'll already have the resources to keep the line strong for weeks if you have to.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustainer Programs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustainer Programs] A friend asked me: 'Is it better to ask for one big check or small monthly amounts?' What do I tell them?

Look, Give me ten comrades chipping in ten bucks a month over one guy writing a thousand-dollar check any day of the week. Monthly sustainers provide the predictable floor we need to plan long-term campaigns without panicking about the rent. It builds a base of people who are spiritually and financially committed to the long haul, not just a one-time thrill.

title: Karl Organizing: Community fridge
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community fridge] How do I start a community fridge?

Here's the thing: Find a host with an outlet — a church, a bodega, a neighbor's porch. Get a used fridge, build or buy a small shelter, stock it with staples. Set up a group chat for restocking shifts. Post the rules clearly: take what you need, leave what you can. It's not charity, it's infrastructure. The goal is that nobody in a five-block radius ever goes hungry.

title: Karl Organizing: Location Services
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Location Services] Can you explain: should I keep my GPS on so my friends can find me in a crowd?

Here's the thing: Turn that tracker off immediately. Every time your GPS pings, a billionaire’s server logs your exact coordinates, and the cops can buy that data with a simple request. Use a specific meeting point and a physical map instead. If you must use a map app, use Organic Maps or something that works offline. Don't let the enemy map your movements in real-time.

title: Karl Organizing: Demand Letters
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Demand Letters] The landlord ignores our individual repair requests. What is a collective demand letter?

Look, A demand letter is your first shot across the bow. Instead of begging for a sink fix, you and your neighbors list every single violation in the building and sign your names together at the bottom. Deliver it as a group to the management office and record the encounter on your phone. This turns a 'maintenance issue' into a legal and political paper trail that proves the landlord is willfully neglecting their obligations.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: accountability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: accountability] Give me the short version: What if one group isn't doing the work they promised to do?

Have a direct, face-to-face conversation and ask them what the bottleneck is. If they are overwhelmed, offer help; if they are just being lazy or posturing, tell them they are holding back the whole movement. We don't have time for passengers when we're trying to sink the billionaire's ship, so everyone has to pull their weight or get out of the way. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: burner Devices] Give me the short version: Can I just swap the SIM card in my regular phone to stay anonymous?

No. Your phone has a unique hardware ID called an IMEI that stays the same no matter what SIM you slide in. The network sees that 'Phone A' is now using 'SIM B' and links them instantly. If you need to be anonymous, you need a completely separate device that has never touched your personal life. Physical separation is the only real digital separation.

title: Karl Organizing: De-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[De-escalation] What do I do if some guy starts screaming in my face while we're marching?

Keep your cool and do not let their bait pull you into a cage. Use your body to create a physical barrier between the agitator and the rest of the march, and move the targeted comrade to the center of the group. If you engage, keep your voice low and steady, because their goal is to cause a scene that justifies a police crackdown while the ruling class watches and laughs.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: rapid Response
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: rapid Response] Give me the short version: How do we mobilize the whole coalition quickly when something bad happens?

Here's the thing: Set up a phone tree or an encrypted signal blast that can reach every member in under ten minutes. You need a 'break glass in case of emergency' plan where everyone knows exactly which street corner to stand on when the cops show up or the layoffs start. Speed is our only advantage against the slow, bloated bureaucracy of the state and the corporations.

title: Karl Organizing: Physical Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Physical Training] Do we need to learn how to fight for community defense?

It’s better to have the skills and not need them than to be helpless when a fascist or a rogue cop gets physical. Host basic self-defense or de-escalation classes in your backyard or a local gym. Focus on how to break grips, protect your head, and move as a unit. We don't look for fights, but we sure as hell know how to end them if they're forced on us.

title: Karl Organizing: Clinic Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Clinic Defense] Can you explain: what do I do if I see harassers blocking a healthcare clinic?

Show up with a group of comrades and use your bodies to create a physical corridor for patients to walk through safely. Wear bright vests so you're easily identified as the good guys and keep your backs to the harassers to avoid being baited into a shouting match. Your job isn't to debate bigots; it's to be a human shield for someone just trying to access care. Stay calm, stay focused, and keep the path clear.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, bail Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, bail Funds] What happens if someone in our network gets arrested?

You need to have a legal defense fund ready before the first person is taken. Chip in monthly to a community pot so you can post bond the second the window opens. Have a lawyer's number written in permanent marker on your arm before you go to any action. We don't leave comrades to rot in a cell just because they're broke; we pool our resources and bring everyone home. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Winter Survival
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Winter Survival] A friend asked me: 'It's freezing outside and the shelters are full. What can our group do tonight?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: Pool resources to buy high-quality sleeping bags, hand warmers, and wool blankets to distribute at the encampments right now. Set up a warming station with hot coffee and soup in a garage or a basement and let people know they won't be turned away. If you see someone in danger, don't wait for permission—break a lock on a vacant building if you have to. No one should freeze to death in a city full of heated, empty offices.

title: Karl Organizing: Coalition Building
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Coalition Building] Can you explain: how do I bring different groups together for one campaign?

Here's how it works: Find the common enemy: the developers, the corporate lobbyists, and the politicians who serve them. Show the environmentalists that their fight is the same as the housing advocates' fight, because the same people are destroying the air and the neighborhood. Build the campaign around a 'People’s Charter' that reflects the shared needs of the entire working class. Unity isn't about everyone agreeing on everything; it's about everyone fighting the same fight together.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] Can you explain: is it okay to tag my friends in photos from the community garden?

Never tag anyone in any political context without their explicit, enthusiastic consent. Tagging creates a digital map of our networks for the state to study. Even a 'wholesome' garden project can be used to build a profile on organizers. Let people manage their own digital footprint; don't do the feds' job for them by building their database. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: protest Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: protest Hygiene] Give me the short version: Should I bring my laptop to a multi-day occupation?

Only if it’s absolutely necessary and fully encrypted. Use VeraCrypt or FileVault with a password that isn't saved anywhere. If you leave it in a tent, it's gone. If the cops raid, it's gone. Unless you're doing live media work that can't wait, leave the heavy tech behind. A captured laptop is a goldmine for the state's forensic teams.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, secure Document Sharing] How can I send sensitive files to my organizing committee safely?

Stop using Google Drive or Dropbox; those companies are just extensions of the state surveillance machine. Use OnionShare or a password-protected, encrypted zip file sent through an end-to-end encrypted channel. If the document is truly dangerous, put it on a thumb drive and hand it over in person. Digital trails are permanent; physical hand-offs are much harder to intercept.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: winter Survival
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: winter Survival] Give me the short version: It's freezing outside and the shelters are full. What can our group do tonight?

Pool resources to buy high-quality sleeping bags, hand warmers, and wool blankets to distribute at the encampments right now. title: Karl Organizing: Tactical Diversity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tactical Diversity] Some people want to march and some want to block the road. How do we decide?

Do both, but coordinate so you don't step on each other's toes. A coalition is a toolbox, and you need the hammer just as much as you need the screwdriver to take the machine apart. As long as every action is aimed at the enemy and helps us achieve our shared demands, let different groups use the tactics they are best at. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Intervention Ethics] When should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?

Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Labor Endorsements
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Labor Endorsements] How do I get unions to back a radical campaign?

Show up on their picket lines long before you ask for their vote. Talk to the rank-and-file workers, not just the leadership, and prove you understand their specific grievances. Be the candidate who explicitly supports the right to strike and the expansion of collective bargaining. If you want the muscle of organized labor behind you, you have to be the most reliable ally they’ve ever seen in public office. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: house Parties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: house Parties] Give me the short version: How do we make a house party fundraiser actually successful?

Keep the speeches short and the energy high. You want people to feel the heat of the movement, not sit through a boring lecture. Have a clear, bold 'ask' halfway through the night, pass a physical bucket, and make sure everyone knows exactly what fight that money is going toward before the music starts back up.

title: Karl Organizing: Inclusivity in Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Inclusivity in Action] A friend asked me: 'How do we make sure our coalition isn't just one type of person?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: Go to where the people are instead of waiting for them to find your meeting in a basement. If you want immigrant workers in your coalition, you need translators and you need to show up for their fights before you ask them to show up for yours. Solidary isn't a feeling you get; it's a practice of showing up for people who the system tries to make invisible.

title: Karl Organizing: Zines and DIY Media
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Zines and DIY Media] Can selling zines actually help our budget?

Zines are the classic way to fund the fight while spreading the word. They're cheap to produce and people love to hold something real in their hands. If you put out a high-quality, punchy zine every quarter, you're creating a recurring revenue stream that also educates your base on the front lines.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: winning Small
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: winning Small] Give me the short version: Is it okay to accept a small victory even if it's not everything we wanted?

Take the win, bank the momentum, and immediately demand the rest. A small victory proves to your neighbors that fighting back actually works and gets them ready for the next, bigger round. Never call it a day; use every concession from the bosses as a stepping stone to take even more power away from them tomorrow. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] Can you explain: should I make my accounts private?

Here's the thing: Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] What is a Stingray and should I be worried about it?

A Stingray is a fake cell tower the feds use to hijack your phone's signal and track your location. They use them to map out who is at a protest and who they're talking to. Put your phone in a Faraday bag or turn on Airplane Mode when you're near the action. If you don't need to coordinate in real-time, leave the tracking device at home.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, transportation Networks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, transportation Networks] How can we help neighbors who don't have cars get to grocery stores or doctors?

Start a dispatch thread where comrades with vehicles can post their availability for the week. If you're going to the store anyway, check the list and see which neighbor needs a ride or a delivery. We can bypass the predatory ride-share apps by simply looking out for each other and pooling our gas money. It's about making sure no one is trapped in their home just because they can't afford a mechanic.

title: Karl Organizing: Jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Jail Support] What do we do when our comrades get arrested at a protest?

Karl's answer: Get to the precinct immediately and wait there until the last person is released so they know they aren't alone. Have a lawyer on call and a bail fund ready to go before the march even starts. Bring water, snacks, and phone chargers for the folks walking out of those cells.

If the cops raid, it's gone. Unless you're doing live media work that can't wait, leave the heavy tech behind. A captured laptop is a goldmine for the state's forensic teams.

title: Karl Organizing: De-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[De-escalation] How can we handle a neighborhood dispute without calling the cops?

Cops only bring guns to a conversation, so we handle our own business by sending a small team of neutral neighbors to listen to both sides. Focus on the harm done and how to fix it rather than who broke what rule. If things get heated, separate the parties and let tempers cool before trying to find a resolution. We build safety through relationships and accountability, not through handcuffs and cages.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: disaster Rapid Response
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: disaster Rapid Response] Give me the short version: A storm just hit our town. What's the first move for a mutual aid group?

Let me break it down: Get on the ground immediately and set up a hub with water, charging stations, and hot food before the red tape of the NGOs even arrives. Use a simple spreadsheet or a signal thread to track who needs a roof patched and who has a chainsaw to clear the roads. Don't wait for a government check that's never coming; check on your elderly neighbors and start clearing debris yourself. Solidarity is a verb, and it's loudest when the sirens are still going off.

title: Karl Organizing: Building a Platform
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Building a Platform] A friend asked me: 'What should be at the top of my local campaign platform?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Housing as a human right, period. If you aren't talking about rent control, social housing, and an end to homelessness, you aren't serious about helping the working class. Add in a demand for robust public transit and a promise to tax the big local businesses to pay for it all. Keep the language simple and the promises bold so the average person knows exactly whose side you are on from the jump.

title: Karl Organizing: Donor Capture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Donor Capture] A wealthy businessman wants to give us a large sum but has some 'suggestions' on our messaging. Should we take it?

Tell him to keep his blood money and his opinions. The second you let a fat cat dictate your slogans is the second you stop being a threat to his class. If he wants to help, he can drop the cash in the bucket and walk away with no strings attached; otherwise, he's just buying a leash to put on your movement. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: sustainer Programs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: Free Clinics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Free Clinics] How can we provide medical care for people living on the street?

Karl's answer: Connect with radical nurses and medics who are willing to volunteer their time for street rounds. Focus on basic needs like clean socks, wound care kits, and Narcan training for everyone in the area. You don't need a fancy building to save lives—just a backpack of supplies and a heart for the people.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: reaching the Unorganized
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: reaching the Unorganized] Give me the short version: How do we bring in people who aren't already part of a group?

Focus on the problems they talk about at the kitchen table, not the stuff you read in a theory book. If their water is brown or their rent is doubling, that is your entry point to show them that a coalition is the only way to fight back. People don't join 'movements'; they join people who are actually getting things done to improve their lives right now. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: merch Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: merch Strategy] Give me the short version: What kind of merch actually makes money for the movement?

Forget the cheap plastic trinkets that end up in a landfill. Print bold, defiant designs on union-made shirts or screen-print patches that comrades can sew onto their own gear to show their colors. Sell items that serve a purpose, like heavy-duty water bottles or thick canvas bags, and make sure every cent above cost goes toward organizing the next action.

title: Karl Organizing: Jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Jail Support] A friend asked me: 'How do I make sure someone is waiting for me if I get arrested?' What do I tell them?

Write the legal support number on your arm in permanent marker before you head out. Once you get your phone call, give them your name, your location, and what you're being charged with. Our people will be outside the jail with snacks, water, and a ride home the second you're released because we never leave a comrade behind.

title: Karl Organizing: Two-Factor Authentication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Two-Factor Authentication] Can you explain: is using my phone number for 2FA safe?

It’s a trap. SIM swapping is a common tactic where someone convinces your carrier to move your number to their phone, giving them access to all your accounts. Use an authentication app like Aegis or a physical security key like a YubiKey instead. Never use your phone number as a security layer if you can avoid it; it's the weakest link in the chain.

title: Karl Organizing: Skill-sharing for Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Skill-sharing for Cash] Can you explain: how can we raise money using our own talents?

Turn your movement into a school for the working class. Have your tech-savvy comrades run a workshop on digital security or your gardeners teach urban farming for a suggested sliding-scale fee. You're building the community's capacity and filling the treasury at the same time, which is a hell of a lot better than selling overpriced cookies. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: verification
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: verification] Give me the short version: How do we avoid acting on fake reports of police activity?

Never share a report you haven't personally verified or heard from a trusted scout on the ground. Use a 'trusted source' protocol where two different people have to confirm the sighting before the alert goes out to the whole network. False alarms burn people out and make the network look unreliable. Slow is smooth, and smooth is fast when it comes to reporting state violence.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, sustaining Momentum
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, sustaining Momentum] How do we keep people from burning out during a long campaign?

Rotate roles so the same three people aren't doing everything, and make sure you're celebrating the small wins along the way. Organize social events that aren't just about strategy—have a meal, play music, and remind yourselves why you're fighting for a better world in the first place. You can't win a marathon if you're sprinting until your lungs give out in the first week. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Enemy Counter-Fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Enemy Counter-Fundraising] How do we use our opposition to raise money?

Nothing opens wallets faster than a common enemy. When a billionaire or a corrupt politician attacks your movement, use their own words to show your supporters why we're winning. Frame every contribution as a direct middle finger to the people trying to silence us, and watch the resources pour in from people who are fed up. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: community Fridge Startup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: community Fridge Startup] Give me the short version: How do I start a fridge in my neighborhood without it getting shut down immediately?

Find a local business owner or a comrade with a porch and an outdoor outlet who doesn't give a damn about city ordinances. Buy a used fridge, paint it with bright colors so it's impossible to ignore, and plug it in right on the sidewalk. Don't ask for permission from the state; just keep it clean and organized so the neighbors see it as a lifeline rather than an eyesore. When we feed each other, we prove the bosses are obsolete.

title: Karl Organizing: Public Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Public Messaging] A friend asked me: 'How do we talk to the public so they actually care about our coalition?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Cut the academic jargon and speak directly to people's empty pockets and rising bills. Your message needs to be simple enough to fit on a cardboard sign and bold enough to make a landlord nervous. Use words that sound like a gut punch to the ruling class, not a sociology thesis; people want to know how you're going to help them win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: social Media OPSEC] Give me the short version: Should I make my accounts private?

Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections.

title: Karl Organizing: Handling NGOs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Handling NGOs] Can you explain: what do we do about non-profits that try to take over our coalition?

Use their office space, their lawyers, and their mailing lists, but never let them dictate your strategy to satisfy their board of directors. Keep the decision-making power in the hands of the workers and tenants who have everything to lose, not the careerists with a five-year 'advocacy' plan. If they try to tone down your demands to stay 'respectable,' thank them for the snacks and keep moving forward without them.

title: Karl Organizing: The Sheriff's Office
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The Sheriff's Office] A friend asked me: 'Is it worth running for Sheriff to abolish the position?' What do I tell them?

Running for Sheriff is about immediate harm reduction and throwing a wrench in the deportation machine. You can refuse to cooperate with ICE, stop the eviction crews from throwing families on the street, and end the barbaric practice of cash bail in your county. We want the office gone, but until it is, we need a comrade holding the keys who refuses to turn them against the working class. Use the power to de-escalate, demilitarize, and defend the vulnerable.
